name: Glendo State Park (Shelter Point Campground)
note: Shelter Point covers an open, nearly treeless point on Glendo Reservoir's south shore beside the marina, with long gravel pads suited to big rigs. The sites sit on a grass bench about 10 m above the high-water line, ending in a cut bank down to the shore, so the lake is in view rather than at the pads; a small day-use beach on the point's south side is reached through the campground. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: reserve.wyoming.gov (US eDirect API wyordr.usedirect.com/wyomingrdr/rdr/, PlaceId 10 'Glendo State Park', FacilityId 345 'Shelter Point', facility point 42.47252778,-104.97724722, read 2026-11-20): 26 web-bookable 'Campsite Non-Electric' SP01-SP26 (IsRVSite true; Rate 10.00; MaximumStay 14; 'Unit & Parking Size(ft)': SP01/SP06 160, SP03/SP05 150, SP25 135, SP11/SP18 130, SP02/SP12/SP26 120, SP07/SP22 100, SP04 95, SP08/SP10/SP14/SP19/SP20 80, SP13/SP16/SP21 75, SP09 70, SP17 65, SP24 60, SP23 55, SP15 50; pull-throughs SP01-SP06, SP11, SP12, SP18, SP22, SP25, SP26; gravel pads, SP17 paved ADA; 'Shade: None' on every site) + a day-use shelter LHDS ($50, 'Day Use') -> real drive-in RV campground; every site is 50 ft or longer, so a 23-ft rig fits all of them. Wyoming State Parks' Shelter Point page (wyoparks.wyo.gov/index.php/about-our-campgrounds/1707-shelter-point-glendo, read as search-result text 2026-11-20; the site refuses with an F5 challenge) and its copies on The Dyrt and Campflare (read 2026-11-20): '26 campsites with gravel parking pads'; 'sits on a peninsula above the high water line'; 'easily accessible by an established gravel road'; 'designed to accommodate large camping units'; 'The campground has very little tree cover, so all sites have little, to no shade'; neighbours the Marina (no ramp of its own). No 4WD, sand or rig-size restriction in the park text (unlike 15 Broken Arrow / 15742 Red Hills). Imagery 2026-11-20: a gravel main road along the point with gravel spurs and pull-throughs, toilet buildings and a shelter, matching the engine's unit points. Not in the DB: no 'Shelter Point' name match; nearest entries 15743 Sagebrush 0.79 km W (FacilityId 342; its SB01 ~0.4 km from SP02) and 6352 Two Moon 1.69 km E (FacilityId 347 at 42.47205,-104.95472; its westernmost unit is ~0.9 km east of SP26), each its own engine facility; 13969 Custer Cove (FacilityId 336) 1.55 km N across the water. Public (state): no price gate.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-20: Esri World Imagery and USGS 3DEP (elevation.nationalmap.gov 3DEPElevation exportImage, F32) fetched in the identical EPSG:3857 square frame at 330 m (0.66 m/px) and two 110 m (0.22 m/px) half-widths, with every reserve.wyoming.gov unit point (grid MapInfo, FacilityId 345) plotted and the full-pool contour drawn; all images rendered. Imagery shows the reservoir somewhat drawn down (a pale beach 15-40 m wide below the full-pool line). Glendo full pool 4635.0 ft = 1413.51 m NAVD88 (glendo_notes.txt); lidar hydro-flattened water 1412.98 m. Unit points sit 1422.4-1428.9 m on lidar, 9-15 m above full pool, and 20-125 m from the nearest full-pool crossing (SP14 20 m, SP26 27 m, SP15 30 m, SP23 31 m, SP10/SP25 33 m, SP17/SP19/SP21/SP24 35-37 m, SP20/SP22 40-41 m, SP09 42 m, SP18 49 m, the rest 65-125 m). Profiles north from the nearest spur ends at 0.22 m/px: SP24 spur end 1423.3 m, full pool at 23 m (1422.3 at 10 m -> 1419.3 at 15 m -> 1413.0 at 25 m); SP23 1423.7, full pool at 33 m (1421.4 at 20 m -> 1415.0 at 30 m); SP10 1424.7, full pool at 30 m (1421.1 at 20 m -> 1413.3 at 30 m); SP14 area 1423.8, full pool at 35 m; SP15 1423.2, full pool at 41 m; SP19-SP21 49-63 m. Ground check: the pads sit on an open grass bench with scattered junipers and no treeline; the bench slopes gently for 15-25 m and then falls 4-9 m in a dark eroded cut bank whose toe is the full-pool line (visible on imagery along the whole north shore of the point), then the beach. Park text: 'sits on a peninsula above the high water line'; Campflare's copy: 'unobstructed views of Glendo Reservoir'. -> sites on a bench atop a cut bank, climb-down not walk-across (bluff/bench rule) -> lakeview; the open view holds from every north-row site. The south-side day-use beach by the marina is a used strip, not a site apron. Engine tags every Shelter Point site 'Waterfront Setting: Reservoir' (type-level; the day-use shelter 'None'). Not below the dam: the point is on the reservoir side, ~1 km west of the dam.
